definition: To hate or detest intensely.
sentence: I abhor raisins in cookies because every raisin is a tiny betrayal pretending to be chocolate.

definition: Extremely miserable, degraded, or hopeless.
sentence: After forgetting his lines, losing his shoe, and walking into the scenery, Kevin's school-play debut was an abject disaster.

definition: To free someone from blame, guilt, or responsibility.
sentence: The security footage absolved the dog of stealing the pie and implicated Grandma with devastating clarity.

definition: To approach and address someone boldly or aggressively.
sentence: A man dressed as a squirrel accosted me outside the supermarket to demand my position on acorns.

definition: The ability to make quick, accurate judgments and decisions.
sentence: Maya showed business acumen by selling umbrellas five minutes before the school's sprinkler system malfunctioned.

definition: Refusing to change one's mind; firm and unyielding.
sentence: Dad was adamant that he did not need reading glasses, although he had just complimented a fire hydrant on its sweater.

definition: Highly skilled or proficient.
sentence: My cat is adept at opening cabinets, ignoring commands, and locating tuna from three zip codes away.

definition: To warn or reprimand someone firmly.
sentence: The librarian admonished us for whispering too loudly, which felt like being arrested for speeding on a tricycle.

definition: Skillful, clever, and quick in movement or thought.
sentence: With one adroit motion, Grandma caught the falling cake, saved the candles, and blamed Uncle Ted.

definition: Difficulty, hardship, or misfortune.
sentence: We faced adversity when the Wi-Fi failed for nine minutes and several family members began learning one another's names.

definition: A natural liking, connection, or similarity.
sentence: My brother has a mysterious affinity for stray cats, broken electronics, and foods that stain permanently.

definition: Having a great deal of money or wealth.
sentence: The affluent poodle arrived at the dog park in a sweater that probably had its own financial adviser.

definition: Cheerful readiness and quick willingness.
sentence: I accepted the offer of free pizza with such alacrity that my chair continued spinning after I had left the room.

definition: To make pain, difficulty, or a problem less severe.
sentence: To alleviate my headache, I turned off my brother's trumpet and experienced an immediate medical miracle.

definition: Distant, reserved, or seemingly uninterested in others.
sentence: The cat remained aloof during the party, observing us from the bookshelf like a disappointed minor deity.

definition: Something placed in a time period where it does not belong; something outdated.
sentence: A knight checking his smartwatch in the medieval movie was a glorious anachronism.

definition: Comparable in certain important ways.
sentence: My father's relationship with the printer is analogous to an ancient blood feud, except with more toner.

definition: Strong hostility or resentment.
sentence: There has been lasting animosity between our cat and the vacuum cleaner since the Incident of 2024.

definition: Something that differs from what is normal or expected.
sentence: Dad voluntarily asking for directions was such an anomaly that Mom checked the calendar for eclipses.

definition: A strong feeling of dislike or aversion.
sentence: I developed an immediate antipathy toward the alarm clock when it expressed opinions at 6:00 a.m.

definition: Self-confidence and composure, especially in a difficult situation.
sentence: She handled the exploding birthday cake with remarkable aplomb, calmly extinguishing it before asking who had invited the pyrotechnician.

definition: Known or understood by very few people; mysterious or obscure.
sentence: The remote control had become so arcane that only Grandpa knew which sequence of seven buttons produced television.

definition: Very enthusiastic, passionate, or devoted.
sentence: He is an ardent supporter of breakfast and has written several strongly worded letters opposing its cancellation.

definition: Requiring great effort; difficult and tiring.
sentence: The arduous journey from my couch to the refrigerator involved twelve feet, one staircase, and tremendous personal courage.

definition: To find out something with certainty.
sentence: I opened the refrigerator to ascertain whether the cake was still there and discovered a crime scene of crumbs.

definition: To attack physically, verbally, or with overwhelming force.
sentence: The moment I opened the door, I was assailed by three puppies, two hugs, and a smell suggesting someone had burned garlic.

definition: Showing persistent, careful effort.
sentence: Through assiduous study, Leo memorized every state capital and somehow forgot where he had put his shoes.

definition: Showing sharp judgment and insight.
sentence: The astute toddler realized that saying "Daddy said yes" works best when Daddy is not in the room.

definition: To make amends for wrongdoing.
sentence: To atone for eating my sister's dessert, I offered her half of mine, which was generous because I had already eaten most of it.

definition: Having a strong interest or enthusiasm for something.
sentence: Grandpa is an avid birdwatcher who can identify forty species but still calls every text message "an email."

definition: Playful, teasing conversation.
sentence: Our friendly banter ended when Grandma said my haircut looked "brave," and nobody could tell whether she was joking.

definition: To explain or discuss something excessively; also to attack repeatedly.
sentence: I will not belabor the point, except with this seventeen-slide presentation titled "Why You Left the Milk Out."

definition: A person who gives money or help to support someone or something.
sentence: Our mysterious benefactor donated enough money for new band uniforms and, for reasons unknown, one enormous gong.

definition: To leave property to someone in a will; to pass something on.
sentence: Grandpa bequeathed me his antique watch and my cousin his legendary collection of motel soaps.

definition: To scold or criticize angrily at length.
sentence: The coach berated the vending machine for stealing his dollar as though it were an athlete who had missed practice.

definition: Very obvious and done without shame or concealment.
sentence: My brother's blatant attempt to steal my fries involved moving them onto his plate while maintaining eye contact.

definition: Cold, empty, depressing, or offering little hope.
sentence: The snack cabinet looked bleak: one stale cracker and a packet of raisins nobody had touched since 2018.

definition: Noisy, energetic, and cheerful.
sentence: The boisterous children turned a quiet picnic into something resembling a small Viking invasion.

definition: Bold and shameless, especially in wrongdoing.
sentence: The raccoon made a brazen theft of my sandwich, then sat on the fence and ate it in front of me.

definition: Shortness of speech or writing.
sentence: In the interest of brevity, Dad summarized our six-hour road trip as "traffic, rain, goat."

definition: Abrupt or blunt in manner or speech.
sentence: The brusque receptionist greeted me with "Name?" in a tone suggesting vowels cost extra.

definition: To grow or develop rapidly.
sentence: My nephew's interest in dinosaurs began to burgeon until every family conversation somehow involved the Cretaceous period.

definition: Emotionally insensitive and showing little concern for others.
sentence: It was callous of my brother to eat the last cupcake while I was giving a speech about how much I wanted it.

definition: Mutual trust, friendship, and good feeling among a group.
sentence: Nothing builds camaraderie like six adults trying together to fold a fitted sheet.

definition: To surrender or stop resisting.
sentence: After forty minutes of arguing with the toddler, Dad capitulated and allowed the stuffed giraffe to have its own airplane seat.

definition: Something that causes or speeds up significant change.
sentence: The arrival of free doughnuts was the catalyst that transformed our sleepy meeting into a highly motivated organization.

definition: Strong official criticism or condemnation.
sentence: The council censured the mayor after he used the emergency siren to announce that his cat was missing.

definition: Embarrassment or distress caused by failure or humiliation.
sentence: To my chagrin, I spent ten minutes searching for my phone while using its flashlight.

definition: To force someone to do something through pressure or threats.
sentence: My niece coerced me into playing tea party by explaining that refusal would be "very disappointing to the princess council."

definition: Clear, logical, and convincing.
sentence: Her cogent argument for getting a puppy included exercise, responsibility, and a suspiciously professional pie chart.

definition: Characteristic of informal everyday speech.
sentence: "Gonna" is colloquial; apparently my English teacher prefers that I announce, "I am going to obtain pizza."

definition: Something that completes or enhances another thing; to do so.
sentence: The garlic bread perfectly complemented the pasta and completely destroyed my chances of polite conversation afterward.

definition: Willing to follow rules, requests, or directions.
sentence: The dog was surprisingly compliant once he realized every command ended with cheese.

definition: To behave as though one is superior to others; also to lower oneself to do something.
sentence: The twelve-year-old condescended to explain smartphones to Grandpa, who had helped design satellites.
synonyms: patronize; talk down to; stoop; deign

definition: Pleasant, friendly, and well suited to one's tastes.
sentence: The book club was congenial until someone casually admitted she folds page corners.

definition: A person with expert knowledge and refined judgment, especially in art or food.
sentence: My six-year-old calls himself a chicken-nugget connoisseur and rejects any dinosaur shape with insufficient anatomical accuracy.

definition: General agreement among a group.
sentence: After three hours, the committee reached consensus that the three-hour meeting had been unnecessary.

definition: Sudden anxiety or dismay, especially at something unexpected.
sentence: There was widespread consternation when the substitute teacher announced that the class hamster was "somewhere in the building."

definition: Likely to cause argument; argumentative.
sentence: The question of whether pineapple belongs on pizza became so contentious that Grandma adjourned dinner.

definition: Genuinely sorry and remorseful.
sentence: The dog looked contrite after stealing the roast, although he continued chewing during the apology.

definition: A difficult problem or puzzling question.
sentence: I faced a conundrum: the remote was under the sleeping cat, and the cat controlled both television access and household peace.

definition: Secret or hidden, especially deliberately.
sentence: Our covert midnight snack mission failed because Dad brought the loudest bag of chips manufactured by science.

definition: To strongly desire something belonging to someone else.
sentence: I coveted my neighbor's new grill so intensely that I began complimenting it by name.

definition: Too ready to believe things without enough evidence.
sentence: My credulous uncle forwarded an article claiming onions can charge cell phones and immediately bought forty pounds of onions.

definition: Large, awkward, or difficult to handle.
sentence: The cumbersome inflatable kayak required two people to carry and four people to explain why it was inside the elevator.

definition: To reduce, shorten, or restrict.
sentence: The principal curtailed the talent show after the third student attempted fire juggling.

definition: A scarcity or lack of something.
sentence: There was a dearth of volunteers after the email mentioned "early Saturday morning" and "manual compost turning."

definition: To expose a false belief or claim.
sentence: The veterinarian debunked Grandpa's theory that the cat was "part panther" by pointing out that he weighed nine pounds and feared cucumbers.

definition: Skillful, quick, and precise.
sentence: With a deft flick of the wrist, Grandma flipped the pancake and caught it on Grandpa's plate three feet away.

definition: Causing harm or damage.
sentence: Eating an entire cheesecake before jogging had a deleterious effect on both my speed and my worldview.

definition: To describe or mark something precisely and clearly.
sentence: The treaty delineated which side of the couch belonged to each sibling and established a neutral cushion zone.

definition: Quiet, modest, and reserved in behavior or appearance.
sentence: She looked demure in the family portrait until you noticed the slingshot hidden behind her back.

definition: To strongly disapprove of or regret something.
sentence: Grandma deplores bad table manners but makes an exception when ribs are involved.

definition: To mock or ridicule contemptuously.
sentence: My siblings derided my homemade haircut until Dad walked in and quietly removed his hat.

definition: A ruler or person with absolute, often cruel, power.
sentence: The toddler became a tiny despot after discovering that adults would do almost anything to stop him screaming in a restaurant.

definition: To discourage or prevent someone from acting.
sentence: The "Beware of Dog" sign did not deter burglars, but the photograph of our Chihuahua wearing goggles created uncertainty.

definition: Very small; a shortened or affectionate form of a name.
sentence: The diminutive dog weighed six pounds but barked as though personally responsible for national defense.

definition: Careful and tactful about keeping something private or avoiding attention.
sentence: The discreet waiter quietly informed me that my shirt was inside out instead of announcing it over the restaurant speakers.

definition: To speak of someone or something as unimportant or inferior.
sentence: Never disparage Grandma's meatballs unless you are prepared to leave the family group chat.

definition: To make a belief, feeling, or condition disappear.
sentence: The first bite dispelled any illusion that Dad's "experimental chili" was safe for civilians.

definition: To disagree with a prevailing opinion or decision.
sentence: Everyone voted for pizza except Kevin, who dissented and was thereafter regarded with deep suspicion.

definition: Easy to control, teach, or manage; gentle.
sentence: The supposedly docile goat ate the map, escaped the pen, and took command of the picnic.

definition: Cheerful, energetic, and overflowing with enthusiasm.
sentence: My ebullient aunt greeted us at 6:30 a.m. as though sunrise were a surprise party she had personally organized.

definition: Outstandingly or shockingly bad.
sentence: The referee made an egregious error by awarding the goal to a child who was sitting on the bench eating grapes.

definition: Extremely happy and excited.
sentence: I was elated to find twenty dollars in my coat until Mom reminded me that she had lent it to me yesterday.

definition: Highly respected, distinguished, or prominent.
sentence: The eminent professor had published six books but still required assistance opening the conference-room coffee dispenser.

definition: The ability to understand and share another person's feelings.
sentence: I felt empathy for the dog after his bath because I too have been betrayed by people claiming something was "for my own good."

definition: To imitate someone in order to equal or surpass them.
sentence: I tried to emulate Grandma's pie crust and instead created a structural material suitable for bridge repair.

definition: Mysterious and difficult to understand.
sentence: The enigmatic note on the refrigerator read only "Tuesday. Pickles. Don't ask."

definition: A perfect example of a particular quality or type.
sentence: Uncle Ron is the epitome of confidence: he gives driving directions in cities he has never visited.

definition: Calmness and emotional balance, especially under stress.
sentence: Mom maintained remarkable equanimity when the blender lid flew off and redecorated the ceiling with blueberry smoothie.

definition: To use vague or ambiguous language to avoid committing to the truth or a position.
sentence: Asked whether he had eaten the cake, my brother equivocated: "I interacted with the cake in several ways."

definition: Incorrect or based on error.
sentence: My erroneous belief that the meeting was casual became apparent when I arrived in shorts and everyone else was wearing suits.

definition: To deliberately avoid or abstain from something.
sentence: I eschew reality television because my own family already provides unlimited unscripted conflict.

definition: To irritate or frustrate intensely.
sentence: Nothing exasperates Dad like the printer displaying "PC LOAD LETTER," a message he considers a personal insult.

definition: Unreasonably or excessively high, especially in price.
sentence: The airport charged an exorbitant price for a sandwich that appeared to have been assembled during the previous administration.

definition: Overflowing with energy, excitement, or joy.
sentence: The exuberant puppy greeted me as though I had returned from a twenty-year voyage instead of taking out the trash.

definition: The front of a building; figuratively, a false outward appearance.
sentence: His facade of confidence collapsed when the waiter asked whether he wanted sparkling or still water.

definition: Achieved or expressed easily, sometimes too simplistically.
sentence: His facile solution to traffic was "Everyone should just drive somewhere else."

definition: To understand something deeply or figure it out.
sentence: I cannot fathom why my cat demands the door opened and then stands in the doorway conducting philosophical research.

definition: Possible and practical to accomplish.
sentence: Building a swimming pool on the roof sounded feasible until someone mentioned gravity, money, and laws.

definition: To pretend to have a feeling, condition, or appearance.
sentence: The child feigned sleep so convincingly that he occasionally opened one eye to check whether we were impressed.

definition: Likely to change loyalties, preferences, or feelings suddenly.
sentence: My fickle toddler loved peas on Monday, hated them Tuesday, and by Wednesday insisted she had never met a pea.

definition: Not showing proper seriousness or respect.
sentence: When asked about the broken window, his flippant response was, "Good news: the baseball definitely works."

definition: Inspiring respect or fear because of great strength, difficulty, or ability.
sentence: Grandma is a formidable Scrabble opponent who keeps a dictionary beside her chair like a medieval weapon.

definition: Courage and endurance in the face of hardship.
sentence: It took tremendous fortitude to continue assembling the furniture after discovering the instructions were entirely pictorial.

definition: Not serious, useful, or sensible; trivial.
sentence: Buying a tiny tuxedo for the hamster seemed frivolous until we received the wedding invitation.

definition: Careful and economical with money or resources.
sentence: Grandpa is so frugal that he washes disposable forks and refers to restaurant napkins as "free household linens."

definition: Secretive and trying to avoid notice.
sentence: The dog's furtive walk away from the kitchen would have been more convincing without the entire roast in his mouth.

definition: Incapable of producing a useful result; pointless.
sentence: Trying to keep white furniture clean with three children and a chocolate Labrador was a futile experiment.

definition: Excessively talkative, especially about unimportant things.
sentence: Our garrulous taxi driver explained his childhood, dental history, and views on zucchini before we reached the second traffic light.

definition: Fluent and confident in a superficial or insincere way.
sentence: His glib assurance that he could fix the sink ended when he asked which part was the sink.

definition: Impressively large or important in a way that may be exaggerated or unrealistic.
sentence: My nephew's grandiose plan for a lemonade stand included a board of directors, valet parking, and international expansion.

definition: A long, forceful, angry speech.
sentence: Dad delivered a harangue about thermostat settings so passionate that the thermostat itself seemed ashamed.

definition: Arrogantly superior and disdainful.
sentence: The haughty poodle refused the ordinary dog biscuit and waited for something with visible truffle shavings.

definition: A person whose beliefs strongly oppose accepted doctrine or convention.
sentence: At our family barbecue, anyone who prefers well-done steak is treated as a culinary heretic.

definition: A pause or break in an activity or sequence.
sentence: My exercise program entered a brief hiatus in February and is now approaching its third anniversary.

definition: Highly distinguished, famous, or admired.
sentence: The illustrious scientist had won three major awards and still wore two different socks to the ceremony.

definition: About to happen very soon.
sentence: The silence from the children's room suggested that either sleep or catastrophe was imminent.

definition: Unable to be changed.
sentence: Grandma's rule that nobody leaves hungry is immutable, possibly protected by constitutional amendment.

definition: Showing no emotion or reaction.
sentence: The poker player remained impassive even when a pigeon landed on his head.

definition: Perfect and free from faults or errors.
sentence: His impeccable suit remained flawless until the chocolate fountain developed ambitions.

definition: Suggested or understood without being stated directly.
sentence: There was an implicit rule that nobody mention Uncle Steve's karaoke performance while he was still holding the microphone.

definition: To beg someone urgently or desperately.
sentence: I implored the mechanic to save my car, which responded by dropping another mysterious piece onto the floor.

definition: Boldly disrespectful or rude.
sentence: The impudent squirrel stole my bagel, sat three feet away, and appeared to critique my reaction.

definition: Unintentional or accidental.
sentence: My inadvertent reply-all informed the entire office that I thought the meeting could have been an email.

definition: Silly, pointless, or lacking sense.
sentence: We spent twenty minutes in an inane debate about whether cereal is technically soup.

definition: Continuing without stopping.
sentence: The child's incessant question "Are we there yet?" began before we had backed out of the driveway.

definition: Unwilling or unable to believe something.
sentence: I was incredulous when Dad claimed he had eaten only one chip while holding an empty family-size bag.

definition: Angry because something seems unfair or insulting.
sentence: The cat looked indignant when I moved him from my chair, apparently forgetting whose mortgage pays for it.

definition: Hardworking, diligent, and productive.
sentence: The industrious beaver built a dam before breakfast while I was still negotiating with my alarm clock.

definition: To reach a conclusion based on evidence rather than direct statement.
sentence: From the smoke, sirens, and Dad holding a blackened spatula, I inferred that dinner had encountered difficulties.

definition: Innocent, sincere, and straightforward; lacking worldly sophistication.
sentence: Her ingenuous question—"Why don't politicians just tell the truth?"—caused three adults to stare silently at their shoes.

definition: Existing as a natural or essential part of something.
sentence: There is an inherent risk in letting a toddler carry an open cup of grape juice across a white carpet.

definition: Gradually and secretly causing harm.
sentence: The insidious habit of checking one notification somehow turned into forty-five minutes of watching videos about raccoons.

definition: To suggest something indirectly, often something unpleasant.
sentence: Are you insinuating that my famous casserole is unpopular just because everyone ordered pizza afterward?

definition: Boldly rude and disrespectful.
sentence: The insolent parrot called Grandpa "old man" and then demanded a cracker.

definition: Honesty and strong moral principles; wholeness or soundness.
sentence: Showing great integrity, Leo returned the wallet he found, although he did ask whether there was a finder's-fee dessert.

definition: Fearless and adventurous.
sentence: The intrepid camper entered the dark woods armed with a flashlight, bug spray, and unreasonable confidence.

definition: Belonging naturally and essentially to something.
sentence: The intrinsic appeal of bubble wrap is that every sheet silently begs to be destroyed.

definition: Tired, bored, or lacking enthusiasm after too much exposure.
sentence: After attending six birthday parties in one weekend, the jaded eight-year-old evaluated cake with the severity of a restaurant critic.

definition: Extremely joyful and triumphant.
sentence: The team was jubilant after winning, although half the players still did not understand the rules.

definition: Showing wise and careful judgment.
sentence: A judicious person adds hot sauce one drop at a time; Uncle Pete apparently prefers the volcanic method.

definition: To place things side by side for comparison or contrast.
sentence: The museum juxtaposed a priceless Renaissance painting with a vending machine that kept eating dollars.
synonyms: compare; contrast; place side by side; align

definition: To express grief, sorrow, or regret.
sentence: Dad lamented the demise of his favorite recliner as though it had served bravely in several wars.

definition: Present but hidden or not yet active.
sentence: My latent athletic ability remains extremely well hidden, despite years of searching.

definition: To praise highly.
sentence: The newspaper lauded the chef's creativity before learning that the "deconstructed lasagna" had simply fallen on the floor.

definition: Sluggish, tired, and lacking energy.
sentence: After Thanksgiving dinner, I became so lethargic that changing television channels felt unnecessarily athletic.

definition: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or interest.
sentence: The listless teenager responded to winning a free vacation with a shrug because the announcement interrupted his nap.

definition: Very talkative.
sentence: The loquacious barber finished my haircut in twelve minutes and his story about fishing in forty-seven.

definition: Producing a great deal of profit.
sentence: The child's lemonade stand became surprisingly lucrative after she began charging adults five dollars to avoid hearing her recorder practice.

definition: Generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival or weaker person.
sentence: After crushing me at chess, Grandma was magnanimous enough not to mention it again until breakfast.

definition: Having or showing a desire to cause harm.
sentence: The printer displayed a malevolent red light and swallowed my final sheet of résumé paper before the interview.

definition: Able to be shaped, bent, or influenced easily.
sentence: The clay was malleable; my grandfather's opinion about thermostat settings was not.

definition: An independent-minded person who refuses to follow convention.
sentence: The office maverick rejected the dress code and arrived Friday wearing a cape and excellent boots.

definition: Small, inadequate, or lacking in quantity or quality.
sentence: My meager lunch consisted of three crackers and the emotional memory of breakfast.

definition: To wander without a direct course; to ramble in speech or thought.
sentence: Grandpa's story meandered from his first car to the Roman Empire before anyone remembered the original question.

definition: Ordinary, routine, and lacking excitement.
sentence: The superhero's most mundane duty was sorting recycling, although he did wear the cape.

definition: Nearsighted; figuratively, lacking long-term perspective.
sentence: The company's myopic plan saved twelve dollars today and created a problem requiring three lawyers tomorrow.

definition: Vague, unclear, or poorly defined.
sentence: My weekend plans were nebulous: something involving food, possibly pants, and definitely no alarm clock.

definition: Failing to give proper care or attention.
sentence: Leaving a toddler alone with permanent markers and a white couch was, in retrospect, negligent.

definition: Calm and unconcerned, often surprisingly so.
sentence: He remained nonchalant while the canoe filled with water, casually asking whether anyone had brought towels.

definition: A sentimental longing for the past.
sentence: The dial-up modem sound filled Dad with nostalgia and everyone under twenty with alarm.

definition: A beginner with little experience.
sentence: As a novice cook, I considered smoke an ingredient rather than a warning.

definition: A subtle distinction or variation in meaning, feeling, or expression.
sentence: The toddler had not yet mastered the nuance between "inside voice" and "airport runway announcement."

definition: Unaware of what is happening around oneself.
sentence: Dad remained oblivious to the bird on his hat until strangers began taking photographs.

definition: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.
sentence: The obstinate jar lid resisted Dad, Mom, three neighbors, and finally surrendered to Grandma without explanation.

definition: Slow to understand; not sharp or direct.
sentence: He was so obtuse that when she said, "Please stop calling me," he asked what time would be better.

definition: Suggesting that something bad is likely to happen.
sentence: The ominous words "I tried to fix it" drifted from the basement just before the lights went out.

definition: Burdensome, difficult, or requiring great effort.
sentence: The onerous task of choosing one dessert from the menu caused visible suffering at our table.

definition: To deliberately exclude someone from a group or society.
sentence: After admitting he microwaved fish in the office kitchen, Gerald was ostracized with a speed normally reserved for contagious diseases.

definition: So obvious or intense that it seems almost tangible.
sentence: The tension was palpable when Grandma asked who had put her cast-iron skillet in the dishwasher.

definition: A statement or situation that seems contradictory but may contain truth.
sentence: The cat's greatest paradox is demanding to go outside and then becoming furious when the door is opened.

definition: A model of excellence or perfection.
sentence: According to his mother, Trevor is a paragon of responsibility, except for the three overdue library books currently under his bed.

definition: A person who is rejected or avoided by a group.
sentence: After bringing tuna salad onto the crowded bus, I became a social pariah before the second stop.

definition: Overly concerned with minor rules, details, or displaying knowledge.
sentence: The pedantic waiter corrected my pronunciation of "bruschetta" while the kitchen behind him was visibly on fire.

definition: Feeling or showing sincere regret for wrongdoing.
sentence: The penitent puppy returned one stolen sock, though the location of the other eleven remains classified.

definition: Deeply or dreamily thoughtful, often with a slightly sad mood.
sentence: He looked pensive by the window, contemplating either the meaning of life or whether we had any chips left.

definition: Highly harmful, especially in a gradual or subtle way.
sentence: The pernicious rumor that Friday's test was canceled spread until thirty students arrived completely unprepared.

definition: Directly relevant to the matter being considered.
sentence: The judge asked for pertinent facts, so Uncle Bob's seventeen-minute story about fishing was immediately disqualified.

definition: To read or examine carefully.
sentence: I perused the restaurant menu with the concentration of a surgeon and still ordered the cheeseburger.

definition: The act of promoting others' welfare, usually through generous donations or service.
sentence: His philanthropy was admirable, although donating two hundred inflatable flamingos to the library required further discussion.

definition: The highest point or greatest level of achievement.
sentence: My culinary career reached its pinnacle when three people ate my lasagna and nobody contacted emergency services.

definition: Brief but full of meaning or substance.
sentence: Grandma's pithy advice on marriage was, "Be kind, and never assemble furniture together."

definition: Calm and peaceful, with little disturbance.
sentence: The lake was perfectly placid until Uncle Frank attempted waterskiing and introduced chaos to several ecosystems.

definition: Seemingly reasonable or likely to be true.
sentence: My excuse that a squirrel stole my homework was almost plausible until I added that it drove away in a Honda.

definition: Deeply moving or emotionally touching.
sentence: The reunion was poignant until Grandpa asked whether anyone had remembered to validate parking.

definition: Focused on practical results rather than theory or ideals.
sentence: Her pragmatic solution to the broken umbrella was to wear a trash bag and continue walking.

definition: Unstable, uncertain, or dangerously likely to fail.
sentence: The birthday cake occupied a precarious position atop three pizza boxes and one extremely nervous folding chair.

definition: An earlier event or decision used as an example for later cases.
sentence: Allowing one child to eat ice cream for breakfast set a dangerous precedent that the siblings cited like constitutional lawyers.

definition: In perfect, clean, or original condition.
sentence: The living room remained pristine for almost eleven minutes after the children came home.

definition: A person who supports or advocates an idea or cause.
sentence: Grandpa became a passionate proponent of afternoon naps after conducting seventy years of research.

definition: Narrow in outlook or limited to local concerns; also relating to a province.
sentence: His provincial worldview assumed any restaurant more than ten miles away served "foreign food."

definition: Exceptional skill or ability.
sentence: My athletic prowess is best demonstrated by my ability to trip over objects that are not technically there.

definition: Having a strong, sharp smell or taste; sharply expressive.
sentence: The cheese was so pungent that opening the refrigerator caused the dog to leave the room voluntarily.

definition: To suppress, calm, or put an end to something.
sentence: The teacher quelled the classroom uprising by announcing that anyone still yelling would help clean the glitter closet.

definition: Spreading or growing uncontrollably or unchecked.
sentence: Rumors were rampant after the principal entered school carrying a goat and refusing to elaborate.

definition: A friendly, harmonious relationship marked by mutual understanding.
sentence: The dentist built instant rapport with my son by admitting that flossing is less exciting than dinosaurs.

definition: To express sharp disapproval or criticism.
sentence: Grandma rebuked the dog for stealing bacon, although her tone suggested grudging professional respect.

definition: To restore friendly relations or make two apparently conflicting things compatible.
sentence: The siblings reconciled after discovering they both blamed Dad for finishing the ice cream.

definition: Unnecessary because it duplicates something already present.
sentence: The sign reading "FREE GIFT AT NO COST" was redundant but extremely committed to the message.

definition: To assign someone or something to a lower or less important position.
sentence: After burning the toast six mornings in a row, Dad was relegated to pouring cereal.

definition: To voluntarily give up possession, control, or a claim.
sentence: The toddler refused to relinquish the remote, citing what he called "ancient couch law."

definition: To formally give up, reject, or disown something.
sentence: I renounced junk food at 8:00 a.m. and formally reversed the decision when doughnuts arrived at 8:14.

definition: Fame or widespread respect for achievements.
sentence: The chef gained international renown for a soufflé that remained upright longer than most governments.

definition: Extremely unpleasant, offensive, or disgusting.
sentence: The smell from the forgotten gym bag was so repugnant that even the garbage can declined involvement.

definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty or damage.
sentence: The resilient houseplant survived neglect, darkness, and one accidental watering with lemonade.

definition: Firmly determined and unwavering.
sentence: She remained resolute in her diet until the waiter said the words "warm chocolate cake."

definition: A short period of rest or relief from difficulty.
sentence: The children's nap gave us a blessed respite during which nobody asked "why" even once.

definition: Reluctant to speak or reveal one's thoughts.
sentence: My usually reticent neighbor became unexpectedly talkative when the subject turned to squirrels stealing tomatoes.

definition: Language designed to persuade or impress, sometimes lacking substance.
sentence: The candidate's rhetoric promised prosperity, unity, and apparently much better parking everywhere.

definition: Having excellent judgment and wisdom.
sentence: Grandma's sagacious advice was simple: never argue with toddlers or people carrying leaf blowers.

definition: Optimistic and confident, especially in a difficult situation.
sentence: Dad remained sanguine about assembling the gazebo even after discovering twenty-seven leftover screws.

definition: Grimly mocking, cynical, or scornfully humorous.
sentence: When the tent collapsed in the rain, Maya gave a sardonic smile and said, "Luxury camping is going beautifully."

definition: Severely critical and cutting.
sentence: The critic's scathing review called the musical "two hours of songs searching desperately for a plot."

definition: To examine something very closely and carefully.
sentence: Grandma scrutinized the restaurant bill like a forensic accountant hunting a conspiracy involving appetizers.

definition: The chance occurrence of something pleasant or useful.
sentence: By pure serendipity, I took the wrong exit and discovered a bakery selling doughnuts the size of steering wheels.

definition: Comfort during grief, disappointment, or distress.
sentence: After losing the game, I found solace in the knowledge that the concession stand still had nachos.

definition: Strict, precise, and demanding.
sentence: The camp had stringent rules: no running, no shouting, and absolutely no teaching the raccoons to open coolers.

definition: Seeking to undermine or overthrow an established system or authority.
sentence: The toddler's subversive campaign against bedtime involved hidden flashlights, cracker stockpiles, and whispered alliances with the dog.

definition: To give in to pressure, temptation, illness, or a stronger force.
sentence: I resisted the cookies heroically for six minutes before succumbing to their buttery propaganda.

definition: To form a conclusion from incomplete evidence.
sentence: Seeing muddy paw prints on the sofa, I surmised that the dog had not spent the afternoon studying philosophy.

definition: Likely or easily affected by something.
sentence: I am highly susceptible to advertising that includes the words "limited edition" and a picture of cheese.

definition: Persistent and unwilling to give up.
sentence: The tenacious toddler spent forty minutes trying to open the childproof cabinet and eventually earned an honorary engineering degree.

definition: To prevent someone from accomplishing a goal.
sentence: My attempt to sneak out early was thwarted by the elevator opening directly in front of my boss.

definition: Lasting only a short time; temporary.
sentence: My enthusiasm for jogging was transient, lasting from the purchase of new shoes until the first hill.

definition: Overused and lacking originality or freshness.
sentence: His graduation speech was so trite that the phrase "follow your dreams" appeared to sigh from exhaustion.

definition: Present or appearing everywhere.
sentence: After I bought a yellow car, yellow cars suddenly seemed ubiquitous, as though they had been waiting for my attention.

definition: Polished, sophisticated, and socially confident.
sentence: The urbane host discussed opera and architecture while discreetly kicking a pizza box under the sofa.

definition: Showing intense force, passion, or conviction.
sentence: Grandpa was vehement that pineapple did not belong on pizza and briefly appeared ready to testify before Congress.

definition: Truthfulness or accuracy.
sentence: The veracity of my brother's story became doubtful when the "giant wolf" turned out to be a damp Pomeranian.

definition: A small remaining trace of something that once existed.
sentence: The lone plastic dinosaur under the couch was the final vestige of last week's toddler invasion.

definition: Experienced indirectly through another person's actions or feelings.
sentence: I experienced vicarious terror watching my son climb the rock wall while he experienced actual delight.

definition: To clear someone from blame or prove that they were right.
sentence: The recovered security video vindicated me and revealed that the missing cheesecake had been stolen by a surprisingly agile grandmother.

definition: Having a strong desire for revenge.
sentence: The vindictive goose remembered exactly who had taken its bread yesterday and pursued him across the picnic field.

definition: Attractively lively, energetic, and animated.
sentence: Our vivacious tour guide described the sewer system with enough enthusiasm to make several people consider careers in plumbing.

definition: Loud and forceful in expressing opinions or feelings.
sentence: The vociferous five-year-old objected to bedtime as though arguing a landmark case before the Supreme Court.

definition: Having an enormous appetite or eagerness for something.
sentence: The voracious reader finished three novels before lunch and then attacked the cereal box because it had words on it.

definition: To decrease gradually in strength, size, or intensity.
sentence: My enthusiasm for assembling the bookshelf began to wane around the time I discovered that Step 2 had forty-seven parts.

definition: Playfully unusual, fanciful, or imaginative.
sentence: The whimsical café served tea in flowerpots and gave every sandwich the name of a minor wizard.

definition: Showing gentle sadness or longing.
sentence: Grandpa looked wistful while describing the days when a candy bar cost a nickel and nobody needed twelve passwords to watch television.

definition: Using dry, subtly mocking humor.
sentence: Looking at the collapsed tent, Dad gave a wry smile and said, "Excellent; we've invented outdoor flooring."

definition: The highest point or peak of success or power.
sentence: My social career reached its zenith when the dog chose to sit beside me instead of the person holding bacon.
